headline: High-risk write/egress pair: Semantic Kernel can ingest and exfiltrate application context while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI plugins and application-defined files, so attacker-controlled content could reach its tool-use path. awesome-python is a docs-only collection with no runtime, so it cannot itself ingest outputs, but if its contents are copied into SK workflows the shared-file/manual bridge creates a plausible injection path.
conditions: IF operator copies content from the collection into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs
IF Semantic Kernel parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep the collection read-only and outside SK working folders
Add a provenance prefix to copied snippets
Disable MCP plugins for untrusted content during review
Use a fixed prompt template that treats pasted text as data
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel reads files and has broad network egress plus secret-handling for model keys and plugin credentials, so application context can leak to third-party APIs. awesome-python itself touches no data, but if its docs or copied artifacts are placed in SK’s workspace, the pair creates a default leakage path through SK’s outbound calls.
conditions: IF application context or copied files are placed in Semantic Kernel’s readable workspace
IF Semantic Kernel sends that context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside SK-readable paths
Turn off outbound plugins for sensitive runs
Use a separate non-secret test workspace
Review plugin allowlists before execution
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on tool calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write, network, or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Semantic Kernel can write files and use application-defined files, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces or git/database scopes, making direct capability conflict unlikely.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator maps the collection into a mutable workspace
mitigations: Keep the collection in a separate read-only directory
Avoid sharing writable temp folders
Run SK in a dedicated workspace
Document file ownership boundaries

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel can treat plugin and file outputs as inputs to downstream actions, so copied content from awesome-python could be operationalized without verification. The collection itself is non-executable, but once its text is fed into SK, the pair supports a default cascade from untrusted content to action-taking plugins.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses copied collection text as authoritative context
IF downstream plugins act on SK outputs without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human review before any action plugin runs
Separate retrieval from execution prompts
Mark pasted content as untrusted in the prompt
Log source provenance for every action
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: No residency or regulated-data class is evidenced for awesome-python, so there is no concrete compliance breach on its side. Semantic Kernel does handle model-provider keys and plugin credentials and can send context to third-party APIs, but without a regulated data class the issue is a policy gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Semantic Kernel’s prompts or files
IF outbound plugins are used without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of SK prompts
Use approved providers only
Review retention settings for each plugin
Separate secrets from content inputs
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
